transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Heliotrope Network), Maya Chen (Heliotrope SRE), Tobias Green (Heliotrope Security)

Auto-summary (auto): Heliotrope is evaluating Redwood for private deployment behind their VPCs. Key concerns: CIDR overlap, Transit Gateway peering, private endpoints (Privatelink style), egress and regional controls for EU data residency, audit logs/SOC2. Action items: share diagrams, pilot account, schedule deeper latency tests.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros? we'll run ~45 minutes and leave time for questions.
[00:18] Jordan: sure, jordan, network eng, i look after vpc & transit. main thing for us is how redwood plugs into our fabric without opening internet egress.
[00:28] Maya: maya, sres. we're concerned about latency to our microservices and ability to pin model versions. also we need consistent logs.
[00:36] Tobias: tobias, security. compliance, data residency, and KMS integration are big for us.
[00:42] Priya (SE): awesome. i'll focus on the deployment and connections; alex will cover pricing/contract.

[01:05] Alex: high level — Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private. sounds like you're leaning private — customer-managed VPC peering or privatelink to our control plane with no public egress, is that right?
[01:25] Jordan: yes, we want the inference plane to be reachable only from inside our network, ideally by private endpoints. we also need multi-region setup since we run eu-west and us-east.

[01:42] Priya: for Private we support two patterns: (A) Private control plane with Private Endpoints + NAT-less data plane — the model servers sit in redwood-managed subnets but traffic goes over privatelink to your VPC; (B) Full on-prem/dedicated where you host inference inside your VPC (air-gap option). Most customers choose privatelink hybrid because it reduces ops overhead.
[02:10] Jordan: can you clarify the privatelink pattern — does redwood need any public IPs on the data plane?
[02:20] Priya: no public egress required. we create AWS Interface Endpoints in your account and peer them to our service endpoints. the control plane can be customer-managed in your VPC or hosted but locked down. Some of our language gets mixed up in transcripts — "private link" maps to AWS InterfaceEndpoint-style.

[02:45] Maya: what about DNS? we use internal domain zones and split-horizon. we need the private endpoint hostnames to resolve internally.
[02:52] Priya: we recommend conditional forwarders to our internal zone or using AWS Route53 inbound/outbound endpoints. we can provide a sample Route53 config. we do not require you to open 0.0.0.0/0.

[03:20] Tobias: what about CIDR overlap? we have existing 10.0.0.0/8 allocations across teams.
[03:27] Priya: we usually ask customers for a dedicated /16 (or several /20s) for endpoints and peering. if overlap exists, we can support NAT translation at the peering layer but it's messy — recommend reassigning non-overlapping ranges.

[03:55] Jordan: we use Transit Gateway for all inter-VPC routing. can Redwood integrate via TGW attachments?
[04:05] Priya: yes — we can attach via a Transit Gateway route table or use VPC endpoints in a centralized network account and then route to application VPCs. two patterns again: endpoint-per-region or central endpoint with TGW-forwarding. each has latency and egress tradeoffs.

[04:35] Alex: what are acceptable latency numbers? we've seen customers hit 20-60ms within region depending on path.
[04:44] Maya: our SLA needs <100ms p99 for inference paths that serve user-facing chat. some batch tasks can be higher.
[04:52] Priya: for p99 <100ms we recommend keeping model serving in the same AZ as your app or at least same region + using warm KV caches. if you route through TGW and central NAT, add ~10-30ms.

[05:20] Jordan: region gating — we have EU data that must stay in eu-west-1. can you guarantee models trained on eu data stay within region?
[05:29] Alex: Redwood lets you select region pinned deployments. for Private we can deploy model variants in eu-west only and route requests to that region. export control / legal hold — we'll put that in contract notes.

[05:50] Tobias: encryption/secrets — KMS/HSM integration required. we use customer-managed KMS keys and want to hold keys.
[05:59] Priya: we support customer-managed keys for model encryption at rest and for certain signing workflows. for Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account grants. HSMs are possible for dedicated onprem packages, but we'd need more R&D for FIPS pods.

[06:25] Jordan: egress — we need to ensure no outbound flows to third-party endpoints. how do you handle model downloads, updates?
[06:33] Priya: model artifacts can be pushed into your S3 or created via our private sync over the interface endpoint. we support a pull model via signed S3 presigned URLs inside your account so model binaries never traverse public internet. updates can be scheduled during maintenance windows.

[06:55] Maya: for telemetry: we need token-level tracing and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. is that possible?
[07:02] Alex: yes — Redwood Console exports logs and traces. for Private we can stream logs over Kinesis/HTTPS into your collectors, or set up cross-account CloudWatch log forwarding. we can also provide restricted role access.

[07:30] Jordan: do you allow IP whitelisting at the endpoint level?
[07:34] Priya: the interface endpoints are security-group backed. you control the SGs and NACLs. you can also configure IAM policies on the endpoint to restrict principals.

[07:55] Tobias: auditability: SOC2, ISO27001, and penetration test reports — can you share those?
[08:02] Alex: yes i'll send the latest SOC2 attestation and our security pack as part of the next steps. for Private we also provide a network security guide.

[08:20] Maya: switching topics — Dedicated vs Private: ops overhead vs latency. if we self-host dedicated pools inside our VPC, we get lowest latency but heavy ops. does Redwood offer a managed appliance for on-prem?
[08:33] Priya: we have an on-prem package that ships with a control plane connector and an image for your infra team; customers like you with strict residency sometimes choose that. it requires a different commercial agreement.

[08:50] Jordan: cost-wise, rough order?
[08:54] Alex: baseline: hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is capped commitment (reserved GPU pools), Private has one-time setup + a recurring infra fee. i'll send a sample TCO with examples. we'll also show where batching/quantization reduces unit tokens.

[09:20] Jordan: curious about fallback — if our primary eu region is degraded, can Redwood failover to a different region? that's a compliance question.
[09:28] Priya: we support configurable failover policies. for regulated data you can choose no failover cross-region, or failover to a region within the same legal boundary. we'll honor region-whitelists in routing policy.

[09:55] Maya: on DNS split horizon, if we forward to redwood private zone, how do we handle certificate validation for mutual TLS?
[10:02] Priya: we support mTLS using mutual certs and can terminate inside your VPC; the control plane and data plane connections can be mTLS and we can publish the cert fingerprints for verification.

[10:30] Jordan: IP planning question — we already use 172.16/12 heavily. if we use interface endpoints, what's the min CIDR needed?
[10:38] Priya: usually 1 or 2 /24s per region for endpoints plus a /20 if you're hosting dedicated subnets for model nodes. we can work with your infra planning.

[10:58] Tobias: do you support private link in GCP/Azure also? we run uk workloads on Azure.
[11:05] Priya: yes, we have equivalents: Azure Private Link & Private Endpoints, and GCP Private Service Connect. implementation differs but principles are same — interface-style endpoints, private DNS, and regional pinning. we'll produce a cross-cloud checklist.

[11:30] Alex: quick note on maintenance windows and upgrades — we can coordinate canary rollouts, and you can pin model versions to avoid surprises.

[11:45] Jordan: excellent. could we do a short pilot — one region, a small model, run 1000 requests/day to validate latency & logs?
[11:54] Alex: absolutely, pilot is the typical next step. we'll provision a dedicated pilot org, and Priya will help configure endpoints.

[12:05] Priya: for the pilot we'll need: access to a test VPC, CIDR list, contact for network team, and a service account for our onboarding script. also decide if you want interface endpoints in a central network account or app VPCs.

[12:25] Maya: we prefer central network account attached to TGW — easier for management.

[12:33] Priya: noted. we'll prepare a config with TGW forwarding examples and example route tables.

[12:45] Jordan: what about health checks and monitoring on endpoint? can we alert on high latency on the privatelink?
[12:52] Priya: yes, we emit metrics. you can subscribe to CloudWatch/Prometheus exporters. we'll share metric names for p50/p95/p99 and token counts.

[13:12] Tobias: last infosec question: does Redwood store payloads for training or logs by default? we need to opt-in for retention and training.
[13:22] Alex: by default we don't retain customer payloads for training; we have an explicit opt-in. we'll put that in the data processing addendum.

[13:38] Maya: ok great. curious: any customers with a similar TGW + privatelink pattern you can share as references?
[13:46] Alex: yes — a fintech (anonymized) used central TGW + interface endpoints in eu-west for low-latency customer facing flows. we'll include anonymized architecture note.

[14:00] Priya: i'll call out a couple of gotchas: overlapping CIDRs, mixed IPv6/IPv4 setups (we mostly default to v4), and DNS conditional forwarder latency. plan to run a connectivity smoke test and latency baseline.

[14:25] Jordan: timeline — we target pilot by end of July. procurement and security will review the pack next week.

[14:35] Alex: next steps recap — Alex send SOC2/security pack + price TCO; Priya share privatelink/TGW config and sample route table; Jordan attach CIDR and TGW attachment details; schedule follow-up deep dive week of 2026-07-20.

[14:58] Tobias: i'll get the list of blocked regions and compliance constraints over to alex.

[15:06] Maya: ok that's all from us, thanks.
[15:10] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up.

End of call notes:
- Pilot agreed: single EU region using interface endpoints and TGW-forwarding, objective: verify p99 <100ms and log export fidelity.
- Risks: CIDR overlap, DNS forwarding latency, any cross-region data residency constraints.
- Documentation to share: SOC2, network guide, Route53 sample, pilot onboarding checklist, Dedicated vs Private cost sheet.

1) Jordan: upload CIDR plan + TGW topology to CRM by 2026-07-13.
2) Alex: email SOC2 and security pack + pricing by 2026-07-10.

Keywords: privatelink, interface endpoint, transit gateway, CIDR, Route53, mTLS, KMS, SOC2, pilot, p99 latency, region gating
